title: Cracking the Safe
description:
# Cracking the Safe

A safe is protected by a password of length `n`. Each password digit is in the range `0` to `k - 1`.

When you keep typing digits, the safe checks only the last `n` digits entered. If those last `n` digits equal the password, the safe opens.

Return any string with minimum possible length that is guaranteed to open the safe no matter which password was chosen. Equivalently, every possible length-`n` password over the `k` digits must appear as a contiguous substring of your returned string.

## Example 1

**Input:** n = 1, k = 2

**Output:** "01"

**Explanation:** The one-digit passwords are "0" and "1", and both appear. "10" is also valid.

## Example 2

**Input:** n = 2, k = 2

**Output:** "00110"

**Explanation:** The length-2 substrings are "00", "01", "11", and "10", covering every binary password exactly once. Other De Bruijn rotations such as "01100" are also valid.

## Constraints

* `1 <= n <= 4`
* `1 <= k <= 10`
* `k^n <= 4096`

solutions.name: Recursive Eulerian Circuit over String Nodes
solutions.description:
## Approach

Model every length n - 1 suffix as a graph node. Appending one digit creates a directed edge whose label is a length n password. Run postorder DFS in Hierholzer style so each edge is used once, then append the start suffix.

## Key Insight

The safe only cares about the last n digits, so each newly traversed edge contributes exactly one new password window. An Eulerian circuit over all k^n edges gives the shortest possible string.

## Complexity Analysis

There are k^n edges. String slicing costs up to O(n) per edge, so the time complexity is O(k^n * n). The visited edge set and recursion stack use O(k^n * n) space.

solutions.name: Iterative Hierholzer Stack
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use the same De Bruijn graph, but replace recursion with explicit stack frames. Each frame remembers the next digit to try from that node; when a frame has no unused outgoing edge left, append the digit that led into it.

## Key Insight

Hierholzer's algorithm is postorder: a digit is emitted only after all edges reachable through that digit have been consumed. The explicit stack preserves that invariant without relying on the Java call stack.

## Complexity Analysis

Each of the k^n edges is pushed and popped once, and each string edge has length n. Time is O(k^n * n), and the visited set plus stack use O(k^n * n) space.

solutions.name: Numeric Euler Circuit
solutions.description:
## Approach

Encode each length n - 1 node as an integer in base k. The edge for appending digit d is node * k + d, and the next node is that edge modulo k^(n - 1). Run the same Euler DFS over integer states.

## Key Insight

The graph structure is identical to the string version, but numeric encoding avoids allocating substring nodes and fixed-length edge strings.

## Complexity Analysis

Every edge is visited once, giving O(k^n) time. The boolean edge array and recursion stack use O(k^n) space.

solutions.name: FKM Lyndon Word Generation
solutions.description:
## Approach

Generate the De Bruijn cycle by concatenating Lyndon words whose lengths divide n, using the Fredricksen-Kessler-Maiorana recurrence. Then append n - 1 zeroes to turn the cycle into a linear safe input string.

## Key Insight

The Lyndon-word construction lists exactly the necklace representatives needed for a De Bruijn sequence. It reaches the same minimum length without explicitly traversing graph edges.

## Complexity Analysis

The recurrence emits k^n symbols in total, so the time complexity is O(k^n). The working array has O(n * k) slots and the output itself has length O(k^n).

solutions.name: Visited Window Backtracking
solutions.timeComplexity: O(k^n * k) practical, exponential backtracking worst case
solutions.description:
## Approach

Start with n zeroes, marking that password as seen. Repeatedly append a digit only when the new last n digits form an unseen password. Backtrack if a choice cannot complete all k^n windows.

## Key Insight

The output string is valid exactly when every sliding window of length n is a different password. This version states that invariant directly, which makes it useful as a teaching bridge from brute force to De Bruijn graphs.

## Complexity Analysis

With the standard digit order it behaves like a De Bruijn construction on the official constraints, visiting O(k^n) windows. In the abstract backtracking model the worst case is exponential. The seen set stores O(k^n) windows of length n.
